Professional AI Image Generation Prompt (Highly Detailed & Precise)
Prompt:
Create a masterpiece-quality, ultra-photorealistic lifestyle portrait in a 4:5 vertical composition, captured in 8K Ultra HD with extraordinary realism, premium editorial photography quality, cinematic HDR lighting, natural skin texture, and exceptional micro-detail. The image should seamlessly blend real-world photography with expressive monochrome hand-drawn sketch art, creating the illusion that the illustrated version of the subject has stepped out of her imagination onto the wall beside her.
The scene takes place inside a modern, warm-toned minimalist home with soft beige walls, polished ivory marble flooring, and elegant Scandinavian-inspired wooden furniture. On the left side of the frame is a light oak wooden cabinet with framed botanical artwork and a small green indoor plant, contributing to a calm, cozy, contemporary atmosphere. A woven jute rug occupies the foreground, enhancing the home's natural aesthetic.
The primary subject is a beautiful young South Asian woman standing naturally beside a plain wall. She has a soft oval face, warm wheatish-fair complexion, expressive dark brown eyes, delicately arched eyebrows, a small straight nose, naturally pink lips, and subtle everyday makeup. Her dark brown hair is loosely tied into a casual low ponytail with soft face-framing strands falling naturally around her cheeks.
She wears an elegant pastel lavender embroidered Indian kurta set featuring intricate white floral thread embroidery throughout the fabric. The kurta has a round neckline, full-length semi-sheer sleeves with embroidered cuffs, matching straight pants, and traditional embroidered jutti flats. Small floral earrings, a delicate gold chain necklace, and minimal accessories complete the refined ethnic look.
The woman leans gently against the wall with a shy, playful posture. Her hands are softly clasped together in front of her body, shoulders slightly raised, one leg bent backward with only the toe touching the floor, creating an adorable, feminine pose. She gazes affectionately toward the illustrated version beside her with a subtle smile, conveying warmth, innocence, and curiosity.
Occupying the right half of the composition is a large monochrome ink sketch of the same woman drawn directly on the wall. The sketch perfectly matches her hairstyle, facial features, clothing, jewelry, proportions, and overall identity while transforming her personality into a lively cartoon-style illustration. The drawing is created using expressive black ink lines, loose cross-hatching, confident brush strokes, and sketchbook-style detailing.
Unlike the real subject's reserved pose, the illustrated character is energetic and playful. She balances on one leg with the opposite leg lifted backward, sticks out her tongue mischievously, winks one eye, and raises both hands making cheerful peace signs. Around the drawing are small hand-drawn doodles including hearts, stars, sparkle icons, motion lines, and playful accent marks that enhance the whimsical personality without overwhelming the composition.
The lighting is soft natural window light from the left, producing smooth shadows, beautiful dimensionality, realistic skin tones, subtle fabric translucency, and gentle highlights on the embroidery. The sketch should appear naturally integrated into the wall with crisp black ink contrast while remaining clearly hand-drawn rather than digitally rendered.

Interested in how frontier labs pre-train image/video generation models?
We were too.

Since those recipes are rarely made public in full, we started from the most mature pretraining playbook available in the open: how modern LLMs are built.
Introducing Chimera: a visual generation model family that brings LLM-style hybrid linear attention and scaling co-design to visual generation.

In large-scale pretraining, nearly every design choice eventually shows up.
That means solving architecture design and scaling as one coupled problem: every architectural choice changes how the model scales, and scaling behavior determines which choices actually survive.
Chimera approaches both jointly, building a model family that remains predictable as model size, compute budget, and data distribution change.

Our key architectural observation is a simple division of labor: a single raster-ordered KDA stream carries long-range state, while modality-aware short convolutions preserve native local geometry.
Together, they form an effective and elegant linear-attention backbone for multidimensional visual data, with periodic MLA providing direct global interaction and sparse MoE expanding capacity at controlled activated compute.

This design comes with a useful effect: NoPE.
In Chimera, position is represented by the computation itself. KDA’s ordered recurrence and learned state decay encode order and recency, while the short convolutions encode local spatial-temporal structure.
Explicit positional embeddings are not needed in our design.
Because these mechanisms are not tied to a fixed training grid or sequence length, Chimera shows strong zero-shot extrapolation in both space and time.
Trained exclusively on 1K images and 5-second videos, it directly generates coherent 4K images with little visible quality degradation and 30-second videos with only 6.5% FID degradation over the final five seconds, all zero-shot, without resolution- or length-specific finetuning.

But architecture alone is not a pretraining recipe unless it scales predictably.
Thus, scaling should not be treated as an afterthought: fitting a curve over model sizes is easy; making that curve meaningful is much harder.
If every model size is differently under-tuned, your scaling law may simply be measuring optimization error.
We propose HeteroP to transfer proxy-tuned hyperparameters module by module across width and depth, giving us a consistently tuned model family. This allows us to fit Chinchilla-style laws over activated model size, training tokens, and the image-video data mixture.

The laws not only provide the reference for compute-optimal model and data size, but also suggest that visual generation may be more model-hungry than we tend to assume.
Under the same parametric loss-fitting method used in Chinchilla, compute-optimal model size grows as FLOPs^0.516 for images, compared with FLOPs^0.46 for language. Video is even more model-hungry, with the exponent rising from 0.516 for images to 0.544 for video.
Guided by these laws, we trained an 11B-parameter Chimera that activates only 2B parameters per token, using ~600 H100 days.
- It matches Wan-2.1 2B pretraining loss with 7.3x fewer FLOPs, and runs 2.14x faster than full attention at 255K tokens.
- It matches FLUX.1-dev and Z-Image-Turbo on GenEval and outperforms both on DPG-Bench, using roughly 20× less training compute than Z-Image-Turbo.

Ultimately, Chimera indicates that once you pretrain at scale, every decision shows up.
And if the Kimi K3 recipe caught your attention, Chimera may look oddly familiar, except the tokens are pixels and frames with diffusion models.

this is what gemini has to say about this:

"Yes, the Explorative Modeling (XM) paper explicitly acknowledges and cites this line of research!

The paper you linked (arXiv:2004.03590) by Ke Li et al. is built on Implicit Maximum Likelihood Estimation (IMLE), which Li originally introduced in 2018. The authors of the XM paper cite the foundational IMLE paper, and Ke Li himself recently posted on X (formerly Twitter) pointing out that XM and IMLE share the exact same motivations and underlying math.

The XM authors write: "Structurally, XMs generalize IMLE... both minimize the expected distance from each data point to its nearest model output."
While the core mathematical objective—finding the closest generated candidate to a real data point to avoid mode collapse—is virtually identical, there are two major differences in implementation and application.

1. Implementation: Global Pool vs. On-the-Fly Generation

 * IMLE (The 2020 paper): IMLE generally works by maintaining a massive, shared global pool of generated samples. During training, it uses a fast approximate nearest-neighbor search to match every real data point in the dataset to the closest sample in that giant pool, and then pulls the model toward that match.
 * Explorative Modeling (Forward XM): Instead of keeping a global pool of old samples, Forward XM generates a fresh batch of K candidates on the fly for each specific data point at every single training step. It simply picks the best of those K candidates right then and there.

2. Application: Standalone Networks vs. A Universal Scaling Axis

 * IMLE: The 2020 paper used this loss to train single-step, feed-forward models (acting as an alternative to GANs) for specific computer vision tasks, like image super-resolution or turning semantic layouts into images.
 * Explorative Modeling: The breakthrough of the XM paper isn't necessarily inventing the loss function, but proving it can be used as a "third pretraining axis" for modern foundation models. Rather than just training single-step models, they inject this K-candidate exploration loop directly into the training of massive multi-step diffusion, flow-matching, and autoregressive models. They showed that scaling K alongside parameter count and dataset size universally improves FLOP and sample efficiency across text, video, and images, which was not known during the original IMLE research.

In short, IMLE laid the exact mathematical groundwork for this "winner-takes-all" coupling. Explorative Modeling simplifies the memory overhead (swapping the global pool for per-step K candidates) and scales it up to act as a multiplier for modern diffusion and transformer architectures."

I wanted to see whether MiniMax H3 could keep a polished campaign aesthetic consistent across an entire scene.

So I gave its Omni Reference feature a clear visual direction: a classic pink car, a well-dressed couple, and a matching pink bag.

The final shot has the man waiting beside the car while the woman opens the trunk and retrieves the bag.

What impressed me was how well the details stayed connected. The characters, car, styling, color palette, and product all felt like parts of the same campaign, rather than separate AI-generated elements.

MiniMax H3 supports text, image, audio, and video references in one workflow, with native 2K generation up to 15 seconds.
